articles.summary: Raytheon-Rafael joint venture ramps up air defense munition production EAST CAMDEN, Ark., Oct. 9, 2026 – Raytheon-Rafael Protection Systems (R2S) has delivered the first Tamir interceptors produced at its new manufacturing facility in Camden, Arkansas, marking the start of U.S. production for the combat-proven Iron Dome Weapon System. Raytheon is an RTX business. Opened in late 2025 after a large capital investment, the Camden facility quickly stood up production as the first site outside Israel to manufacture Tamir interceptors. With operations underway, R2S is scaling output to meet growing Israel and U.S. demand for short and medium range air defense, a market that continues to grow amid evolving global security requirements. “For the first time, we can produce these interceptors in the United States,” said Jonathan Casey, R2S Chief Executive Officer. “Domestic production strengthens our industrial base and provides the U.S. and its allies with another reliable, scalable source for these critical defensive systems.” In addition to Israeli Tamir interceptors, the Camden facility is planning to produce the U.S. variant of Tamir in support of the U.S. Marine Corps’ Medium Range Intercept Capability, further strengthening the defense of both Israel and the United States. About Raytheon Raytheon, an RTX business, is a leading provider of defense solutions to help the U.S. government, our allies and partners defend their national sovereignty and ensure their security. For more than 100 years, Raytheon has developed new technologies and enhanced existing capabilities in integrated air and missile defense, smart weapons, missiles, advanced sensors and radars, interceptors, space-based systems, hypersonics and missile defense across land, air, sea and space. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact corporatepr@rtx.com. About RAFAEL RAFAEL Advanced Defense Systems Ltd. designs, develops, manufactures and supplies a wide range of high-tech defense systems for air, land, sea, and space applications for the Israel Defense Forces and the Israeli defense establishment, as well as for customers around the world. The company offers its customers a diversified array of innovative solutions at the leading edge of global technology, from underwater systems through naval, ground, and air superiority systems to space systems. RAFAEL is one of Israel's three largest defense companies, employing over 11,000 people and numerous subcontractors and service suppliers, including in the United States.
articles.title: R2S delivers first U.S. produced Tamir interceptors

articles.summary: New 6500 square-meters (70K square-foot) facility will support growing demand for commercial and military engines RZESZÓW, Poland (Oct. 23, 2026) – Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, today announced the start of construction on a new $100 million (375 million zloty) facility to increase production capacity, introduce manufacturing of critical rotating components and meet the growing global demand for commercial and military engines, including the Pratt & Whitney GTF™, F135 and F100 engines. The expanded site is expected to become operational in 2028, creating more than 120 jobs. The Rzeszów site provides advanced manufacturing and technology development capabilities for commercial and military engines, turboprops and auxiliary power units. Its work includes the producing critical engine components such as the GTF fan drive gear system, F100 static structures and key F135 parts. The site also manufactures engines for helicopters, business jets and general aviation aircraft — specifically those from the PT6, PW200, PW500/600 and PW800 families.
articles.title: RTX’s Pratt & Whitney initiates construction of new $100 million Rzeszów expansion to strengthen advanced manufacturing capabilities

articles.summary: Software‑driven upgrades to increase range and efficiencyPORTSMOUTH, R.I., Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has been awarded a contract from the Office of Naval Research (ONR) to develop advanced target‑detection capabilities for naval radar systems.Under the contract, Raytheon's Advanced Technology team will develop and evaluate advanced signal and data-processing algorithms and integrate targeted software upgrades to significantly extend detection range, increase sensitivity and improve radar-system efficiency. These enhancements will undergo rigorous laboratory and field testing to validate performance and operational use, preparing them for transition into Raytheon's SPY‑6 family of radars and other future naval radars.

articles.summary: New launcher supports Army modernization with improved capabilityTUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The U.S. Army awarded the Javelin Joint Venture (JJV), a partnership between Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, and Lockheed Martin, a $215 million production contract for Lightweight Command Launch Units, or LWCLU. The LWCLU, the next-generation launcher for the Javelin® weapon system, is replacing its legacy command launch unit.The Javelin LWCLU is designed to be adaptable and compatible with all current, past and future Javelin variants. The award comes five months after the JJV delivered the first LWCLUs to the Army.

articles.summary: Sweden to integrate Landshield and Landshield Plus systems on military platforms LONDON, (Oct. 21, 2026) – Raytheon UK, part of RTX's (NYSE: RTX) Raytheon business, has been awarded contracts from the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration's (FMV) Commercial Affairs Division to provide Landshield and Landshield Plus GPS anti-jamming systems for Swedish military platforms. The Landshield family of systems strengthens assured positioning, navigation and timing (APNT) capabilities and protects critical GPS signals from electronic warfare threats in contested environments. Landshield and Landshield Plus combine advanced anti-jam technology with a compact, platform-agnostic design for use across land, maritime and air platforms. Landshield Plus incorporates an antenna and anti-jam processor in a single unit, providing real-time awareness of interference sources and helping operators maintain reliable navigation.
articles.title: Raytheon UK to strengthen NATO navigation resilience with GPS anti-jamming technology

articles.summary: New digital systems will improve detection and long-term performanceWOBURN, Mass., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has been selected to modernize U.S. Space Force radar sites that serve as the outermost layer of the nation's missile‑defense architecture. These strategic sensors provide early warning of launches, characterization of objects and activity tracking in space.Through the Ground-Based Radar Digitization (GBRD) program, Raytheon will work with the Space Force to modernize long‑serving systems, strengthening domain awareness and supporting a more resilient, layered security architecture. The program will modernize and upgrade existing systems to enhance overall performance, improve reliability, and support more advanced operational capabilities.These updates will help ensure the radars continue to provide critical ground-based early warning and space monitoring capabilities for decades to come.

articles.summary: Raytheon funding development of Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrades to defeat the latest advanced drone threatsTUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, successfully completed three tests of its new Coyote® Block 2C+RM upgrades, advancing the program from concept to testing in just 15 months. These Raytheon-funded developmental testing events show rapid progress of current Coyote Block 2C+RM interceptor upgrades to support an urgent joint U.S. military mission to counter evolving drone threats.The Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrade builds on the combat–proven performance of current Coyote variants, which have intercepted hundreds of drones. This effort intends to integrate a rocket motor for faster launch and flight, along with a new seeker and warhead designed to defeat all classes of current and emerging drone threats.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon completes three successful tests of new Coyote upgrades

articles.summary: Amendment adds full FlightSense™ coverage to airliner’s narrowbody fleet SINGAPORE (Oct. 12, 2026) – Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has expanded its contract with Vietjet Air to include FlightSense™, which provides technical and maintenance solutions for the airline’s additional 44 GTF-powered Airbus A320neo family aircraft. Under the amendment, FlightSense will deliver guaranteed component availability, reduced downtime and cost predictability, enhancing the reliability and operational efficiency of the airline’s fleet. “FlightSense will enable Vietjet to turn raw data on its A320neo and A321XLR into predictable maintenance needs and improved reliability,” said Jen Latka, vice president of Aftermarket, Power & Controls at Collins Aerospace. “The expansion of FlightSense will help strengthening our engineering administration, optimizing operation and reliability of Vietjet’s fleet, and laying foundation for the airline’s fleet and network expansion plan,” said Michael Hickey, chief operating officer of Vietjet. FlightSense is a full-lifecycle support program powered by Collins’ Ascentia® analytics platform, which helps airlines effectively analyze data, optimize maintenance actions and improve fleet operations. articles.summary: Company investing and scaling production to support global demand TUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, was awarded $729 million to deliver critical components of the LIDS counter-drone system to the U.S. Army, Qatar and Jordan. LIDS – or the Low, slow, small, unmanned aircraft Integrated Defeat System – incorporates Raytheon's Ku-band Radio Frequency Sensor (KuRFS)and the Coyote®effector. These are the first international sales of KuRFS and Coyote. As key elements of the U.S. Army's LIDS program, KuRFS provides advanced 360-degree threat detection, while Coyote low-cost kinetic and non-kinetic effectors defeat individual drones as well as swarms, with hundreds of intercepts in combat. The contract includes a mix of fixed-site and mobile configurations for LIDS.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon awarded $729 million in counter-drone contracts for U.S., Qatar, and Jordan
